workflow_yaml:
name: CI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  checks: write

env:
  APP_ENV: ci

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: sh -xe {0}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon clean build

      - name: Test
        id: test
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon test

      - name: Publish JUnit results
        if: ${{ always() && steps.test.outcome != 'skipped' && steps.test.outcome != '' }}
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v2
        with:
          name: JUnit test results
          path: 'build/test-results/test/*.xml'
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: 'true'
          fail-on-empty: 'true'

      - name: Archive JAR artifacts
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-jars
          path: 'build/libs/*.jar'
          if-no-files-found: error
assumptions: No triggers are specified in the source. workflow_dispatch is an evaluation-only choice, not an inferred Jenkins trigger.

ubuntu-latest is a reasonable Linux choice for agent any. Its Java installation and other tooling are not guaranteed to match Jenkins; the source supplies no JDK version or agent provisioning configuration.
checkout scm is assumed to refer to the workflow repository and selected revision. Jenkins-specific SCM credentials and checkout configuration are unavailable.

Jenkins JUnit publication can mark a build UNSTABLE for test failures. GitHub Actions has no equivalent status, so reported test failures fail the job. The reporting action creates a GitHub check rather than Jenkins test-history pages.

GitHub artifact upload does not reproduce Jenkins fingerprinting or its cross-build provenance tracking. JARs are retained as a downloadable workflow artifact, using GitHub's configured retention rather than unspecified Jenkins retention.
always() requests failure-time and cancellation-time collection, but collection cannot be guaranteed after runner loss or forced termination.

behavior_mapping.source: A single agent runs Checkout, Build, and Test sequentially in one workspace.
behavior_mapping.target: jobs.build-and-test runs ordered steps in one job, preserving workspace contents without cross-job output-transfer assumptions.
Workflow-level env.APP_ENV is ci and applies to commands, reporting, and artifact collection.
The Build step executes the unchanged command. Failure prevents the Test step from running.
The Test step executes the unchanged command after a successful Build, without suppressing command failure.

behavior_mapping.source: Test-stage post always publishes junit 'build/test-results/test/*.xml', including after a failing test command.
behavior_mapping.target: Publish JUnit results uses always() and the Test step outcome, so it runs after an executed Test step but not when Test was skipped. The literal glob is preserved; test failures, parsing failures, and empty reports fail publication rather than merely uploading XML.

behavior_mapping.source: Pipeline post always archives build/libs/*.jar with fingerprint: true; missing artifacts fail by default.
behavior_mapping.target: Archive JAR artifacts runs with always(), including after command or reporting failures. It preserves the literal glob and uses if-no-files-found: error. Jenkins fingerprinting is unsupported, as documented in assumptions.
